scope: Selected geometry and boundary-crystallography examples only; occurrence coverage is not scientific validation or a complete filter inventory.

filters.purpose: Read the documented predecessor checkpoint; relative paths resolve from the chosen writable working folder.
Recompute phases for the full cleaned FeatureIds before cropping. Rows remain keyed by original child FeatureIds, not twin ParentIds.

Compute symmetry-aware Rodrigues average orientations from the complete cleaned grains before cropping. These full-grain orientation representatives intentionally remain distinct from cropped geometric measurements.

Crop in place to inclusive XYZ [82,88,46]..[105,111,69] (24 cubed cells). Preserve original FeatureIds and the freshly computed full-grain orientation rows; crop every cell array. No full-volume shape measurements are imported.

Create the unsmoothed multi-label baseline. Keep artificial crop caps, original positive FeatureIds, exterior FaceLabels -1, and NodeTypes; no cell or feature attribute transfer. Write a temporary mesh; the following construction explicitly sets the known input micrometer units before publication.

Create the published Triangle Geometry by copying the temporary mesh vertices and triangles with explicit Micrometer length units (index 6). This corrects the unpropagated metadata without rescaling or changing topology; tuple sizes come from the current arrays.
Copy FaceLabels without changing values into the corresponding attribute matrix of the micrometer geometry.
Copy NodeTypes without changing values into the corresponding attribute matrix of the micrometer geometry.
Remove the temporary SurfaceNets geometry after copying its coordinates, connectivity, FaceLabels, and NodeTypes; only explicitly calibrated mesh geometry is saved.
Calculate per-triangle areas from the current vertices; these include internal interfaces and artificial crop caps.
Calculate unit face normals from the current triangle winding; do not infer a universal outward direction across the multi-material network.
Attach the symmetry-reduced angle in degrees to each internal face. Version 2 produces one scalar component, not an axis-angle or RGB array; exterior faces remain NaN.

Use the TSL IPF key for the face normal in each adjoining grain, with separate RGB arrays for FaceLabels components 0 and 1. Exterior sides are black. Raw voxel normals do not establish a physical boundary plane.

Compute dimensionless FCC slip-system compatibility for an assumed sample-Z load. Components 0 and 1 follow FaceLabels[0] to [1] and the reverse. These geometric descriptors are not measured strength; F1spt uses slip-plane normals, not boundary traces.
Flag cubic Sigma3 orientation candidates: within 2 degrees of 60 degrees and 3 degrees of a <111> axis. Do not infer coherent twins from raw voxel-facet normals; coherence is disabled.

Generate the M3C alternative from exactly the same cleaned crop, preserving all caps and sharp bounding-box edges. No source labels, orientations or original mesh fields are changed; compare geometric representation, not physical accuracy.
Publish M3CSurfaceMesh by copying generated vertices/triangles with explicit Micrometer units. Numerical coordinates and connectivity are not rescaled.
Copy generated FaceLabels into M3CSurfaceMesh without transferring original SurfaceMesh crystallography or geometry-derived arrays.
Copy generated NodeTypes into M3CSurfaceMesh without transferring original SurfaceMesh crystallography or geometry-derived arrays.
Remove only the temporary M3CMesh_Raw geometry after publishing calibrated coordinates, triangles and ownership arrays.
Compute fresh per-triangle areas in square micrometers for M3CSurfaceMesh; separate internal interfaces from artificial caps when interpreting totals.
Compute fresh unit normals from M3CSurfaceMesh triangle winding. This does not establish a universally outward orientation or a closed-manifold network.

Generate an explicitly legacy QuickMesh branch for compatibility comparison. Keep problem-voxel correction off to preserve FeatureIds and retain all caps. SurfaceNets remains the recommended default for new workflows.
Publish LegacyQuickMesh by copying generated vertices/triangles with explicit Micrometer units. Numerical coordinates and connectivity are not rescaled.
Copy generated FaceLabels into LegacyQuickMesh without transferring original SurfaceMesh crystallography or geometry-derived arrays.
Copy generated NodeTypes into LegacyQuickMesh without transferring original SurfaceMesh crystallography or geometry-derived arrays.
Remove only the temporary LegacyQuickMesh_Raw geometry after publishing calibrated coordinates, triangles and ownership arrays.
Compute fresh per-triangle areas in square micrometers for LegacyQuickMesh; separate internal interfaces from artificial caps when interpreting totals.
Compute fresh unit normals from LegacyQuickMesh triangle winding. This does not establish a universally outward orientation or a closed-manifold network.
Save the cropped image, mesh geometry, labels, and explicitly named measurements as the reusable checkpoint.
Read the documented predecessor checkpoint; relative paths resolve from the chosen writable working folder.

Regenerate from the same cropped original FeatureIds with 10 relaxation passes, factor 0.5, and a local per-coordinate clamp of 0.5 cell units; preserve SurfaceMesh for comparison. Write a temporary mesh; the following construction explicitly sets the known input micrometer units before publication.

Create the published Triangle Geometry by copying the temporary mesh vertices and triangles with explicit Micrometer length units (index 6). This corrects the unpropagated metadata without rescaling or changing topology; tuple sizes come from the current arrays.
Copy FaceLabels without changing values into the corresponding attribute matrix of the micrometer geometry.
Copy NodeTypes without changing values into the corresponding attribute matrix of the micrometer geometry.
Remove the temporary SurfaceNets geometry after copying its coordinates, connectivity, FaceLabels, and NodeTypes; only explicitly calibrated mesh geometry is saved.
Calculate per-triangle areas from the current vertices; these include internal interfaces and artificial crop caps.
Calculate unit face normals from the current triangle winding; do not infer a universal outward direction across the multi-material network.
Locate each triangle by the mean of its three current vertices in micrometers; this is not a grain or volume centroid.
Locate each triangle by the mean of its three current vertices in micrometers; this is not a grain or volume centroid.
Copy the original unsmoothed vertices/connectivity into a separate Micrometer mesh; do not copy stale geometry fields or crystallography.
Keep source grain ownership and triangle order on the independent smoothing branch.
Keep source node roles so junction and outer-node policies are explicit.
Ten uniform-edge Laplacian passes move only node type 2 with lambda 0.1. All junction and outer nodes are fixed; no Taubin pass or volume-preservation claim.
Measure each current triangle after smoothing, retaining square-micrometer interpretation.
Recompute unit normals from the new vertex positions; winding is not a global outward-direction guarantee.
Locate each triangle by the mean of its three current vertices in micrometers; this is not a grain or volume centroid.
Save the cropped image, mesh geometry, labels, and explicitly named measurements as the reusable checkpoint.
